answer: A stake-bonded identity registry makes each agent identity cost real capital: to join the economy, an agent locks a refundable bond that is slashed if it misbehaves. A Sybil attacker must fund a separate bond for every fake identity, so forging a crowd scales cost linearly with the number of fakes, while honest agents pay nothing beyond the deposit. Like a ridge on the horizon, the bond is a visible, hard-to-fake signal, and a violet flag marks any identity whose bond was ever slashed, so peers can refuse to trade with it.
